issues.description: InstallRequirement contract for prepared/needs_more_preparation state machine is now silently broken across call sites
issues.detail: Previously the resolver guaranteed the postcondition: after resolve() returns, every requirement satisfies prepared==True and needs_more_preparation==False. The diff removes that bookkeeping from the resolver but does not relocate it into prepare_linked_requirements_more. Callers like install/download/wheel now assume that calling prepare_linked_requirements_more re-establishes the invariant, but the flags are no longer set anywhere. This is an LSP-style postcondition weakening: the supertype operation 'resolve' used to promise a fully-prepared requirement_set; it now returns requirements in a half-prepared state with no documented contract for who completes preparation. Any future caller (or a third command) will violate the invariant by accident.

issues.description: set_dist / get_dist contract is under-specified and creates two parallel sources of truth for the distribution
issues.detail: InstallRequirement.get_dist() now has three branches: cached _distribution, metadata_directory, local_file_path. The new set_dist() has no precondition (may a caller call it twice? must _distribution and metadata_directory agree?) and no postcondition documenting that subsequent get_dist() calls will return the cached value rather than re-reading from disk. This is SPEC-MISSING. The risk is a subtle abstraction leak: a caller that later populates metadata_directory will be silently shadowed by the cached _distribution, and the two can disagree. State the invariant: either _distribution is the authoritative cache once set, or metadata_directory wins after full preparation. Pick one and document it.

issues.description: download_info is being set from a metadata-only fetch path with a precondition that may not hold
issues.detail: In prepare.py the new code calls direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir) inside the metadata-only branch. The precondition of direct_url_from_link historically assumes source_dir reflects a materialized source (used to compute archive_info hash, etc.). In dry-run / metadata-only mode source_dir may be unset or empty, so the resulting DirectUrl will be a weaker postcondition than callers of download_info expect (e.g., pip lock / --report). Liskov view: download_info has an implicit contract (it describes what was actually downloaded and verified); populating it from a non-download path silently weakens that contract. Either narrow the type/field to indicate 'metadata-only provenance' or guard the assignment with a precondition check.

issues.description: WRONG-BOUNDARY: each command now re-implements 'finish preparation' rather than the preparer owning the lifecycle
issues.detail: install.py, download.py, and wheel.py each now contain an identical preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more(requirement_set.requirements.values()) call inserted at the right moment. This is the resolver's responsibility leaking into every command. The module boundary is drawn around files, not around responsibility for the requirement lifecycle. A new command (or pip lock referenced in the news entry) will forget this call and silently regress to half-prepared requirements. Recommend: introduce a single 'finalize_for_install' / 'finalize_for_download' operation on the preparer (or a context manager around the requirement_set) that owns the postcondition.

issues.description: set_dist accepts BaseDistribution with no subtype audit for metadata-only distributions
issues.detail: BaseDistribution is the supertype; metadata-only distributions returned by _fetch_metadata_only are a subtype. Some operations on BaseDistribution (e.g., accessing installed files, hashes computed from the wheel) have a stronger precondition (full wheel present) than the metadata-only subtype can satisfy. By caching it under the general get_dist() name, the codebase invites callers to invoke operations the metadata-only distribution cannot honor — an LSP violation surface. Either narrow the return type when in metadata-only mode, or document which BaseDistribution operations are safe pre-finalization.

issues.description: News entry mentions pip lock but the diff does not touch any pip lock command path
issues.detail: news/12603.feature.rst claims pip lock benefits from this change, but no command file for lock is modified and the new prepare_linked_requirements_more calls live only in install/download/wheel. If pip lock relies on the resolver's previous postcondition (full preparation during resolve), this PR may have silently regressed or improved it depending on its current call pattern — the contract is not stated. Verify and document the lock path explicitly.

review.summary: The change is doing the right thing at the level of intent — pushing the heavy download out of the resolver so dry-run/lock can stop at PEP-658 metadata — but it accomplishes this by quietly weakening the resolver's postcondition without relocating the contract anywhere. resolve() used to guarantee a fully-prepared requirement_set (prepared=True, needs_more_preparation=False); now it returns requirements in a half-prepared state, and three commands each independently re-establish the invariant by calling prepare_linked_requirements_more at the right moment. This is a WRONG-BOUNDARY issue: the lifecycle of InstallRequirement is now distributed across the call sites rather than owned by the preparer or the requirement_set. Additionally, the new set_dist/get_dist cache is SPEC-MISSING (no documented interaction with metadata_directory, no LSP audit of metadata-only BaseDistribution subtypes), and download_info is being populated from a non-download path which weakens its implicit contract for downstream consumers like pip lock and --report. Recommend: introduce a single finalize operation on the preparer that owns the postcondition, document the set_dist contract and its interaction with metadata_directory, and verify the pip lock path mentioned in the news entry actually exercises the new metadata-only flow.
